jobs.title: Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization
jobs.description:
This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.

Job posting ID:
9382

Employment status:
Regular full-time

Position's anticipated start date:
2027-01-25

Salary/Rate of pay:
$132,300 - $155,600

Application deadline:
2026-11-13

This external job posting may close earlier than the advertised deadline. We recommend applying as soon as possible.

Application requirements:

Your up-to-date resume.
Job specific cover letter.
We recommend you save a copy of the job posting for reference throughout the recruitment process.

Do you currently work for Canadian Blood Services? All employees must apply via the internal career page.

Together, the work we do connects people and changes lives — including your own.

Be part of a dynamic, collaborative and caring organization committed to saving and improving lives. Thousands of patients depend on us every day for reliable access to safe blood, plasma, stem cells and organs and tissues.

About The Role

Canadian Blood Services is seeking a Regular Full-Time Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization
to join our Enterprise Portfolio, Program and Project Management Office (ePMO)
team in our Ottawa or Toronto office.

The ePMO
team delivers programs and services that advance valuable organizational initiatives, ensuring they are completed on time and on budget. Our focus is on maximizing business outcomes for Canadian Blood Services and the people in Canada we serve.

As the Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization, you will lead value realization and benefits tracking activities aligned with corporate strategy, corporate funding cycles, and the delivery of high-visibility projects and programs across the organization.

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Program Enablement & Project Management Office, you will lead ePMO-led value realization activities across enterprise programs and provide guidance to support value-informed decision-making. You will contribute to enterprise portfolio management and reporting for all corporate priority projects, including ePMO projects; escalate issues requiring executive attention; and provide leadership to enterprise projects coordinated through process management. You will also ensure compliance with corporate portfolio reporting requirements and support the execution of select projects within the portfolio by fostering collaboration and integration across divisions. In addition, you will provide a challenge function across other ePMO activities, including reporting, automation and artificial intelligence (AI), data and analytics, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Formula for success

Leveraging your skills in ePMO operations, you will oversee value realization driven through programs, providing leadership, coordination, and management of enterprise PMO processes and functions.
Applying your expertise in value realization leadership, you will oversee the development of proposals and business cases, as required, to help articulate anticipated benefits and the value proposition.
Demonstrating your skills in influencing and negotiating, you will motivate and coach staff for high performance, act with transparency, and promote a problem-solving mindset and collaborative culture.
Utilizing your experience in benefits management and performance measurement, you will ensure all centrally delivered projects and programs have defined benefits, measured using key performance indicators, tracked, and communicated in a consistent and effective manner, and incorporate effective change and risk management controls.
Drawing on your skills in project interdependency management and prioritization, you will identify, manage, and address interdependencies between projects and prioritization to drive the greatest value.
Demonstrating your ability to lead with empathy and emotional intelligence, you will apply the advanced soft skills required to lead and motivate others to achieve deliverables, particularly when priorities and expectations may be in conflict.
Contributing your expertise in strategic initiatives and project leadership, you will take a lead role in developing and maintaining various initiatives and participate in special projects and corporate initiatives as assigned by the Director.
Applying your skills in performance improvement and governance, you will identify opportunities to improve performance and apply fit-for-purpose processes that balance governance and empowerment.
Fostering your strengths in people leadership and talent development, you will create a high-performing, engaged, and inclusive team environment by setting clear expectations, developing talent, supporting career growth and succession planning, and promoting continuous learning, collaboration, and professional development.
Applying your analytical and problem-solving skills, you will use your seasoned experience and knowledge to analyze highly complex problems, interpret business needs, and develop integrated, innovative solutions. This will often require deeper investigation of conflicting information and novel thinking to establish solutions.

Desired Education And Skills

A bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Science, Public Administration, Health Administration, or a related discipline. A master’s degree (MBA, MPA, MSc, or equivalent) is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience managing multiple projects and programs involving large teams, significant budgets, and multiple stakeholders, including at the executive level.
Demonstrated ability to build and lead teams, including managing, coaching, and developing project managers, employees, and contracted resources.
Proven ability to manage a significant project portfolio within a large organization, with a focus on value realization and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success in establishing and maturing value-driven portfolios and programs that support organizational transformation and strategic objectives.
Expertise in process transformation and service delivery, including the ability to develop recommendations and present outcomes to executive leadership.
Strong analytical and technical capabilities, with the ability to leverage portfolio reporting, data analytics, performance metrics, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve decision-making, reporting, and operational efficiency.
Knowledge of corporate planning, budgeting, and financial management processes that support effective portfolio management and prioritization.
Familiarity with introducing new products or processes within a regulated environment is considered an asset.
Knowledge of managing and implementing process changes within a unionized workforce environment is considered an asset.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain project and portfolio documentation, reports, business cases, and executive-level presentations.
Familiarity with Agile methodologies and working within Agile teams is considered an asset.
Proficiency with relevant project and portfolio management tools, including Microsoft Project Professional and Microsoft Project Online (MSPO), is considered an asset.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, including collaboration, facilitation, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement.
Strong financial and operational planning capabilities, with the ability to align resources, budgets, and priorities with organizational objectives.

What We Offer You

4 weeks’ vacation.
Comprehensive group health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family.
Annual performance award of up to 10%.
Defined benefit pension plan.
Employee discounts, wellness programs, and access to professional development resources.

What You Can Expect

This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.
You will work Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week, 7.5 hours per day.
Travel is required to attend meetings and to fulfill project commitments.

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply by providing your up-to-date resume. This could be your first step towards a meaningful and inspiring career. Come to work each day knowing that you save lives.

We acknowledge that the work of Canadian Blood Services spans many Territories and Treaty areas across the country, and we are grateful for the Traditional Knowledge Keepers and Elders who have guided us in this important work. We recognize the land and waters that have inspired our work and offer gratitude to those Indigenous peoples on whose territory we work, live and play.

Diversity and inclusion play a vital role in ensuring health equity for patients across Canada. We are committed to reflecting Canada’s population in our organization and fostering an environment where all employees can be their authentic selves, with equal opportunities to succeed and contribute.

We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those considered for an interview or those invited to participate in an assessment will be contacted. Emails are sent directly from our system, to ensure you receive them please add donotreply@blood.ca and system@successfactors.com to your safe senders list.

Applicants who require accommodation should discuss their needs with us.

Ottawa

jobs.title: VP of Digital Marketing (Remote, Quebec City)
jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As VP of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
At SaskTel, big ideas come to life. We're a team of curious thinkers, bold innovators, and problem-solvers who make technology work better for people, businesses, and communities across Saskatchewan. Bring your energy, share your ideas, and help us shape what's next.

Chief Information Officer

SaskTel is entering a defining period of change. As the organization accelerates its transformation into a modern tech-forward communications leader, we are seeking a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who can bring clarity, courage and conviction to a division that sits at the centre of SaskTel’s future. This is a role for a leader who thrives in complexity, sees opportunity in legacy, and understands how to evolve a technology function into a true strategic engine for the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the CIO is accountable for SaskTel’s enterprise technology strategy, digital modernization, cybersecurity posture, data governance, and the delivery of reliable, secure, and efficient technology services. The CIO also serves as SaskTel’s Chief Security Officer and holds enterprise accountability for data governance. This leader will oversee a large, diverse team responsible for enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, architecture, and service delivery. This role requires a leader who can modernize a complex, legacy-heavy environment and ensure they have a high-performing team who is willing and welcoming of the new technology horizon SaskTel is entering into.

The Mandate

For SaskTel, the role goes beyond providing telecommunications services. Technology connects Saskatchewan, strengthen communities, enables businesses and support the province’s economic growth. As technology continues to reshape how we live and work, it is increasingly central to Saskatchewan’s future. This is not a caretaker role. It is a once-in-a-career mandate to modernize, simplify, and elevate a technology environment that underpins every connection SaskTel delivers.

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are a seasoned technology executive with a proven record of leading large, complex organizations through meaningful modernization. You bring deep expertise in enterprise systems, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, and data governance, paired with the leadership presence and elevate information services as a true strategic partner.

You have assembled 15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant time at the senior-executive level, and a history of modernizing legacy environments, improving delivery performance, and driving cultural change. You understand how to strengthen execution, introduce modern development practices, and lead teams through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.

Academically grounded with a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, technology, or a related discipline and you are comfortable operating in regulated or public-sector environments. Experience with large-scale enterprise transformations, including OSS/BSS, CRM, ERP, or cloud-native modernization, is highly valued.

Above all, you are courageous, collaborative, and forward-looking. You bring the courage to challenge entrenched norms, the backbone to make risk-based decisions, and the leadership maturity to reset a long-standing operating model. You build trust quickly, communicate with executive presence, and bring the mindset and energy required to help SaskTel evolve. If you are energized by meaningful transformation, if you thrive in environments where change is both necessary and possible, and if you want your work to matter beyond the balance sheet, this role offers a rare platform to make a lasting impact.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca
. Applications may be submitted confidentially through clicking here. Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan’s leading Information and Communications Technology provider

What makes SaskTel special is our people, and the fun, connected culture we create together. Our highly engaged employees bring diverse perspectives, collaborate across teams, and turn fresh thinking into meaningful results. Experienced leaders are there to listen, coach, and champion your growth, giving you opportunities to take on new challenges, build your skills, and move your career forward. Here, you can be yourself, feel supported, and do work you're proud of alongside people who celebrate ideas, achievements, and each other.

CULTURE AND VALUES

Upholds foundational values of honesty, integrity and respect.

Consistently demonstrates our culture: Think Big (Innovation and Courage), Make a Difference (Commitment and Community), Focus on Experiences (Simplicity and Agility), and working as OneSaskTel Team.

This is an on-site position located at the location(s) above. The successful candidate must be located within the province of Saskatchewan. Out of province/country candidates must be willing to relocate. Flexible work opportunities, in province, may be available.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan's leading Information and Communications Technology provider.

As one of Saskatchewan's Top Employers, we offer rewarding work, competitive salaries, comprehensive health and dental plans, pension plans, flexible work arrangements, paid time off, training & more! For more information on our benefits please click here: SaskTel's Benefits.

We value diversity as a key aspect of our culture. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all candidates to participate fully in the recruitment process. If you need any accommodation at any stage of the process, please contact us confidentially at talent.acquisition@sasktel.com.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
JMC is partnering with LCL Group of Companies
to recruit a Director of Finance
. This full-time, in-person opportunity can be based in Moncton or the Campbellton/Charlo area, New Brunswick, with occasional travel to other offices and project sites.

LCL is a growing, family-owned construction group that builds the roads, water mains, and sewer systems communities depend on. With established operations and continued growth, LCL is looking for a finance leader who can strengthen financial operations, develop its accounting team, and help guide the business forward.

Reporting to the President, the Director of Finance will take ownership of accounting and finance across the group. Working closely with leadership and Operations, you will turn financial information into practical insights, improve systems and processes, and support sound business decisions.

What You’ll Do

Lead accounting operations, month-end and year-end close, financial statements, and consolidated reporting.
Oversee construction job costing, work-in-progress reporting, project forecasts, and margin analysis.
Manage budgets, cash-flow forecasting, working capital, and financial planning.
Partner with Operations to assess project profitability, equipment costs, and capital investments.
Strengthen internal controls, streamline processes, and improve Acumatica ERP and related systems.
Lead and develop the accounting team while managing relationships with external accountants, lenders, and advisors.
Provide financial recommendations that support strategic decisions and continued growth.

What You Bring

At least seven years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including a senior accounting or financial management role.
Experience leading an accounting team and taking ownership of financial operations.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, budgeting, forecasting, and multi-company accounting.
Construction accounting, job costing, and work-in-progress experience are strongly preferred.
Proficiency with ERP systems and Excel. Acumatica experience is an asset.
A CPA designation is preferred, though strong relevant experience will be considered.
A practical, accountable leadership style, with the confidence to challenge assumptions and communicate clearly with financial and operational teams.

To learn more contact Chad Murray at chad@teamjmc.ca
.

jobs.title: AVP, CTR Promo Strategy & Programs
jobs.description:
Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most recognized and trusted companies, with a portfolio that spans retail, financial services, loyalty, petroleum, and real estate. Founded in 1922, CTC includes iconic banners and businesses such as Canadian Tire, SportChek, Mark’s, PartSource, Gas+, Triangle Rewards, Canadian Tire Financial Services, and CT REIT, supported by a national network of retail and gasoline outlets and tens of thousands of people across Canada.

CTC’s purpose is simple and enduring: “We are here to make life in Canada better.” The company continues to invest in technology, data, omnichannel capabilities, customer experience, and enterprise transformation while maintaining a strong connection to communities across the country. Leaders at CTC are expected to operate with integrity, build strong cross-functional relationships, and help advance a culture grounded in accountability, inclusion, innovation, and care for customers, employees, Dealers, franchisees, partners, and communities.

About The Role

The AVP, CTR Promo Strategy & Programs leads the strategy, planning and performance of CTR promotional programs, translating enterprise strategy into customer-relevant, financially productive and operationally executable plans. The role owns CTR promotional choices and governance, leveraging AI-enabled capabilities, while building a high-performing Promotions team.

Accountability spans the weekly promotional program, key promo events, non-product promotions, and integration with key strategic priorities inclusive of customer-centric growth, Triangle loyalty, Digital activation, and other key price value initiatives. The mandate is to deliver best in class CTR promotional programs through offer and price selection that strengthens customer value perception and drives key financial outcomes.

The AVP translates promo strategy priorities into coordinated delivery plans with strong stakeholder management and customer focus. The AVP leads continuous improvement across the function, strengthening workflows, champions automation, and drives disciplined performance management as the promotional ecosystem evolves.

What You'll Do

Lead CTR promotional strategy and deliver performance
Translate CTR Promotions strategy into an annual plan, inclusive of being a change agent for the multi-year price value transformation roadmap as part of True North.
Set the role, depth, frequency, placement and incentive approach for CTR promotions.
Balance promo sales, retail margin, net promo return, Triangle value and customer value perception.
Anticipate and respond to competitive dynamics to direct promotional resources toward higher-impact events and reduce low-ROI or duplicative promotions.Own promotional outcomes by driving solid in-season program communication, risk management, trade-offs, course correction and executive escalation.
Own CTR promo planning and program decisions
Lead product and price decisions for CTR promotional program.
Own product and price selection for key promotional events - IEPs, NPP events, Special Print Programs and Grand Openings.
Manage the CTR promotional calendar and ensure integration across events, categories and channels to maximize business performance and customer impact.
Align promotional plans to category roles, customer needs, key shopping moments and enterprise priorities.
Challenge the status quo, ensuring promo plans reflect customer and competitive signals to differentiate in the market.
Lead CTR promo optimization, governance and performance management
Set objectives, constraints and high-quality business inputs for AI-enabled pricing and promotion engines.
Embed enterprise promo guardrails for depth, frequency, placement and incentives.
Establish planning, in-season and post-event operating rhythms with standardized dashboards.
Reduce exceptions through stronger upfront planning, decision discipline and escalation paths.
Use post-event insights to improve future event, item and price decisions.
Advance AI-enabled promotional capabilities & optimization
Ensure CTR promo process and team readiness for newly launched price value initiatives under the True North strategy.
Develop a promo automation roadmap and prioritize enhancements that improve impact and efficiency.
Provide the CTR business perspective to improve models, tools, guardrails and workflows.

Job Description

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & CFO, Canadian Personal & Small Business Banking (CPSB), the Associate Vice President leads Finance support for Real Estate Secured Lending (RESL), Specialized Sales Force (SSF), Operations and the Chief Operating Officer (COO) organization. The role is the senior Finance partner to the SVP, RESL; SVP, Specialized Sales Force; and SVP & COO, CPSB, connecting strategy with financial outcomes across significant revenue, balance sheet, expense and investment portfolios.

The role provides forward-looking advice and independent challenge on growth, profitability, productivity, transformation and resource allocation. It brings an enterprise perspective to decisions, identifies opportunities for value creation and maintains strong financial management, controls and performance discipline.

As a member of TD's leadership team, the AVP sets high ethical and performance standards, develops talent and collaborates across the Bank to deliver sustainable results. The role requires strategic insight, business acumen, sound judgment and integrity.

Position-specific Accountabilities

Lead portfolio planning, forecasting, reporting and performance management. Develop driver-based forecasts and scenarios, explain variances, and translate risks and opportunities into executive insight and recommended actions.
Advise and independently challenge RESL pricing and offers. Assess volume, retention, margin and risk-adjusted return trade-offs, considering funding costs, customer behaviour and competition.
Lead SSF financial planning and analysis, including MMS and broker channel financials and compensation models. Evaluate acquisition costs, incentives, conversion, retention and lifetime profitability; advise on compensation changes and channel mix across branch, specialist, broker and digital distribution.
Assess portfolio economics across volumes, market share, margins, credit, funding, expenses and returns. Analyze profitability by product, segment and origination cohort, isolating mix, pricing, renewals and runoff. Partner with Treasury, Risk, Product and Distribution on rate scenarios, funding and capital implications.
Advise on investment prioritization and allocation of capital, expense and capacity. Challenge business cases, returns, costs and milestones; track benefits and cross-CPSB dependencies and trade-offs. Recommend reprioritization when economics or delivery assumptions change.
Analyze operational cost drivers, unit costs, cost-to-serve and capacity. Link volumes, service levels, staffing and demand to expense plans; challenge assumptions and identify productivity and operating-leverage opportunities while protecting controls and customer outcomes.
Partner with COO leaders to connect strategic priorities, transformation and operating performance to financial outcomes. Assess cross-business initiatives and execution risks, balancing near-term commitments with longer-term value.
Provide oversight and independent challenge of reporting, controls, allocations and accounting. Reinforce direct and shared cost ownership, reliable management information and consistent financial treatment; resolve issues with Finance and enterprise partners.

Finance Talent, Capability & Leadership

Build a high-performing Finance team with the capabilities to deliver stronger business partnership, insight and independent challenge. Shape talent priorities, attract and develop talent, and strengthen succession and leadership depth, with a focus on commercial acumen, strategic judgment and executive influence.
Advance the portfolio's Finance operating model in alignment with enterprise and CPSB strategy. Shape and implement changes within the team, and strengthen team capacity for higher-value advisory work.
Champion data, digital and AI-enabled Finance, influencing priorities with enterprise partners and accelerating adoption of tools, analytics and automation that improve decision-making, information quality, productivity and colleague capacity. Provide leadership and accountability for a sound financial control environment within the portfolio. Ensure changes to processes, tools and responsibilities maintain clear ownership and effective governance; partner with enterprise control owners to address risks and sustain confidence in financial information.
Lead through the TD Way, creating an inclusive, high-performing culture grounded in clear expectations, accountability, constructive challenge, continuous improvement and colleague development. Set clear objectives, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance gaps Operate as an enterprise Finance leader, building partnerships across CPSB and enterprise Finance, Treasury, Risk, Accounting, Tax, Data & Analytics and Technology; contribute to the broader CPSB Finance agenda beyond the immediate portfolio.

Qualifications & Experience

Significant senior-level financial management, business advisory and leadership experience, with strong banking economics and commercial acumen.
Strong understanding of secured lending profitability, pricing and channel economics, together with operational cost management and investment evaluation; ability to connect product, distribution and operating decisions to financial performance.
Experience evaluating growth, investment, transformation, productivity and resource-allocation decisions, with sound judgment in balancing financial outcomes, customer needs and risk.
Strong analytical and communication skills; ability to synthesize complex issues into concise executive recommendations and influence decisions through constructive challenge.
Proven experience developing talent and succession depth and implementing Finance improvements across team operating models, processes, tools and controls; ability to partner with enterprise teams and deliver sustained adoption and measurable benefits.
Ability to manage competing priorities effectively and maintain resilience in a fast-paced environment.

The Financial Risk Oversight team has overall responsibility within Group Risk Management to provide independent oversight of risk taking and risk mitigation activities related to market and liquidity risk. The team also provides subject matter expertise with respect to market and liquidity risk and how it affects the organization. This role focuses on, but is not limited to, market and liquidity risk oversight for Manulife Bank. The individual will work collaboratively with the Bank Risk function and the General Account to ensure key market and liquidity risks are properly addressed.

Position Responsibilities

Identify and monitor market and liquidity risk independent of Operating Segments and Treasury.
Review and provide constructive input on risk policies including but not limited to Liquidity Management Policy, Interest Rate Risk Management Policy, Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy.
Review the Liquidity Contingency Plan and make recommendations to improve its transparency and efficiency.
Ensure key market and liquidity risks are identified based on regulatory guidance, measured appropriately and incorporated in the overall risk management framework.
Review and validate the risk limits, parameters and assumptions used in various metrics for assessing liquidity risk and interest rate risk.
Monitor exposures against approved risk limits.
Have an expert knowledge of OSFI’s regulations such as the Liquidity Adequacy Requirements (LAR) Guideline, Interest Rate Risk Management Guideline, and ensure appropriate and effective implementation of these key guidelines.
Review and assess methodologies and assumptions for measuring key market and liquidity risk metrics.
Review and recommend stress testing scenarios / assumptions used for stress testing exercises (e.g., bank deposits run-offs).
Review and provide constructive feedback on the Bank’s funding plan.
Provide regular input and effective challenge over the first line of business’ risk management practices including but not limited to risk metrics, limits and methodologies.
Support and provide subject matter expertise to the Bank CRO and General Account Business CRO in areas of market and liquidity risk.
Review and provide input on all regulatory issues relating to market and liquidity risk.
Assess risk positions and risk exposures and steps being taken to address them.
Assess and opine on the adequacy of risk versus return in current portfolio and any proposed strategies.

Required Qualifications

Advanced degree in Finance or another quantitative discipline.
FRM and/or CFA designation an asset.
Ability to communicate effectively (oral and written), build strong working relationships and influence outcomes within and across segments.
Self-starter and ability to work with little guidance.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in the financial services industry, preferably in Treasury, Retail Banking and Insurance
Outstanding analytical and conceptual skills.
Excellent management and interpersonal skills.

Problems/Challenges

Increasing complexity associated with liquidity risk policies and the supporting measurement, monitoring and reporting infrastructure.
Balancing the requirements and expectations of multiple internal and external partners.

Personal Attributes And Cultural Fit

Inspires and motivates others.
Role model of ethics and integrity who builds a culture of respect.
Highly effective change agent who embraces change and leads change management.
Provides courageous advice.
Results-driven; highly focused on accountability.
Ability to handle multiple stakeholders
Demonstrates a commitment to delivering excellent service balanced with appropriate risk management and strategic perspective.
Highly collaborative working style.

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.

A Little Bit About Us

Founded in Vancouver in 2016, FORM is the sports technology company behind the award-winning FORM Smart Swim Goggles. Since launching in 2019, our goggles have earned global recognition, including Red Dot, iF Design, and Global Triathlon awards, and are trusted by professional athletes, age-group triathletes, and swimmers looking to get better.

We're a talented, tight-knit team that's fun to work with and serious about building great products. Together, we bring decades of consumer product experience spanning sports eyewear, interface design, and activity-tracking algorithms.

To learn more, visit formswim.com

The Opportunity

Reporting to the CEO, you'll own FORM's finance function end to end. You'll start by learning how our accounting function runs today, then partner with the team to strengthen controls and streamline processes as we grow. From there, you'll lean into financial modelling and become a strategic partner to the executive team.

You'll work directly alongside the CEO, with access to our fractional CFO for mentorship. You'll have real ownership over how FORM plans, reports, and grows, and the support to step up as the role expands. This role requires a hands-on leader who likes being close to the numbers.

What You'll Own

Lead a two-person accounting team, managing our Senior Accountant and supporting the development of the Accountant on their team
Work with the team to put scalable internal controls in place for accurate, reliable financial statements
Own cash and cashflow planning across short- and long-term horizons
Partner with the executive team to build annual budgets, forecasts, and department-specific KPI reporting
Build financial models and scenario plans to support strategic decisions and fundraising
Support the CEO on investor materials and Board and shareholder reporting
Manage tax, audit, legal, and banking partners, and keep FORM compliant across jurisdictions

What Great Looks Like

Reliable reporting generated in hours, not days
A controls environment the executive team trusts
Budgets and KPI reports that department leads use to run their teams
AI embedded in our finance workflows, so the team spends less time on manual tasks and more on insights

The Landscape

Inventory across multi-warehouse global operations
Multiple entities (Canada and US) and multiple currencies
Startup financing, including SAFEs, convertible notes, and equity and debt rounds

How We Work

Daring - Greatness lies just outside our comfort zone. You bring fresh ideas and aren't afraid to try something new
Focused - We're not afraid of throwing out great ideas to execute the right one. You know which numbers matter most and keep the team pointed at them
Human - Work as a team, work for one another, listen to our members. You make finance approachable and explain the numbers so every FORMie can act on them
Learn Fast, Act Fast - Improve through trial, testing and action. You move with urgency, learn from each cycle, and keep improving how finance works

Required Skills & Qualifications

CPA or equivalent, with 7-10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leading and developing a team in a Director-level role at a growing startup
Experience with hardware and SaaS business models, including a strong understanding of SaaS KPIs
Strong financial modelling skills and the ability to turn data into decisions
A proven record of accurate internal and external financial and KPI reporting in a complex, multi-currency environment
Experience with employee stock option plans (ESOPs), including administration and cap table management
Experience supporting equity and debt financing processes
Canadian, US, and international tax and accounting experience, including Canadian grants and tax credits such as SR&ED
Strong storytelling skills that turn financial data into insights people can act on

Nice to Haves

International (US and Europe preferred)
Consumer electronics, fitness, or wearables experience

Benefits

Group Life - AD&D - Critical Illness Insurance

Employee Discounts

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.

Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As VP of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As VP of Digital Marketing you lead that department. This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.
